name: Quarterly Review
summary: Rhythm-of-business arc for a quarterly team or department update: objectives, wins, progress, financials, challenges, lessons, next-quarter goals, recognition, discussion, conclusion. The team-facing sibling of Weekly Progress; for a leadership business review with asks, use Quarterly Business Review.

beats.name: Objectives
beats.description: Restate what the team committed to at the start of the quarter, with the measure for each. The audience should know what 'on track' meant before they see any results.

beats.name: Success Stories
beats.description: Lead with two or three concrete wins: what happened, who made it happen, and what it changed for customers or the business. Specific and dated beats general and enthusiastic.

beats.name: Progress Overview
beats.description: Score each objective against its measure with a simple status (met, partly met, missed) and the one number that proves it. Let the audience scan the whole quarter in one slide.

beats.name: Financial Performance
beats.description: Show the quarter's key financial metrics against plan and against last quarter: revenue, spend, margin or whatever the team is accountable for. One headline number, then the variance that matters.

beats.name: Challenges
beats.description: Name what did not go to plan and why, without blame. Pair each challenge with what the team is doing about it or the help it needs.

beats.name: Lessons Learned
beats.description: Turn the quarter into insight: what the team now knows that it did not know ninety days ago, and how that changes how it works.

beats.name: Goals Next Quarter
beats.description: Set the next quarter's objectives with a measure and an owner each. Fewer and sharper than this quarter's list is usually right.

beats.name: Highlights & Recognition
beats.description: Recognize specific people and contributions by name. Written recognition in the deck travels further than a mention in the room.

beats.name: Discussion & Feedback
beats.description: Open the floor with two or three framed questions, so the discussion lands on the decisions and trade-offs the team actually needs input on.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Close with the quarter in one sentence and the one thing everyone should do or remember next. End on momentum, not on the agenda.
